answers.M8-S1: The author tests whether his Mason-bees can find their way home from far away, and despite injuries and wind, some return quickly.
answers.M8-S2: To show the bees faced an extra obstacle: they had to fly low and couldn't see the land from above, making their return harder and more impressive.
answers.M8-S3: The bees weren't struggling or lost; they found their way easily enough that they even had time to stop and gather food on the way.
answers.M8-S4: So Aglaé could recognize which returning bees were the ones he had carried away, not other bees from the nest.
answers.M8-S5: He starts out doubtful any bees will make it home, but ends up surprised and impressed that two returned quickly.
answers.M8-S6: In time order, as an account of an experiment: setting it up, releasing the bees, the difficulties, then the result.
answers.M8-S7: To show how fast the bees got home—over two miles in under 45 minutes, even with stopping to forage—proving how well they navigate.
answers.M8-S8: To show the experiment was hard and imperfect; injuries meant fewer bees could make the trip, adding to the difficulty.
answers.M8-S9: That the bees couldn't find home by seeing landmarks from above, so they must use some other way to find their nest.
